name: Fraud Prevention Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal fraud prevention policy governing the identification, investigation, and mitigation of fraud risks across all customer accounts and banking products. The policy is owned by the Head of Financial Crime and applies to all staff, financial crime, risk, and retail banking functions. Effective from 2026-01-15 with annual review scheduled for 2027-01-15.
context: Audience | All Staff, Financial Crime, Risk, Retail Banking

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The executive role responsible for ownership and governance of the Fraud Prevention Policy at FirstUK Bank. This role holds accountability for policy implementation, compliance, and periodic review.

name: All Staff
description: All employees of FirstUK Bank are identified as an audience for the Fraud Prevention Policy, indicating universal applicability of fraud prevention obligations and awareness requirements across the organisation.
context: Audience | All Staff, Financial Crime, Risk, Retail Banking

name: Financial Crime Department
description: The department within FirstUK Bank responsible for administering and enforcing the Fraud Prevention Policy. This department is identified as both the policy owner department and a key audience for policy implementation.
context: Audience | All Staff, Financial Crime, Risk, Retail Banking

name: FCA COBS
description: Financial Conduct Authority Conduct of Business rules that form the regulatory basis for FirstUK Bank's Fraud Prevention Policy. COBS establishes conduct standards and customer protection requirements applicable to the bank's fraud prevention obligations.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS, Payment Services Regulations 2017

name: Payment Services Regulations 2017
description: UK legislation governing payment services and fraud liability that forms the regulatory basis for FirstUK Bank's Fraud Prevention Policy. The PSR 2017 establishes requirements for fraud prevention, customer liability, and payment security.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS, Payment Services Regulations 2017

name: Fraud
description: The primary risk category addressed by FirstUK Bank's Fraud Prevention Policy. Fraud encompasses unauthorised transactions, account takeover, payment fraud, and other deceptive activities that threaten customer assets and bank integrity.

name: Fraud Prevention Policy

context: FirstUK Bank maintains a Fraud Prevention Policy to detect, prevent, and respond to fraudulent transactions and account takeover.
The policy establishes procedures for fraud detection, customer reimbursement, and investigation.

name: Fraud
description: The risk of fraudulent transactions and account takeover that the Fraud Prevention Policy is designed to detect, prevent, and respond to.

procedures for fraud detection, customer reimbursement, and investigation

detect, prevent, and respond to fraudulent transactions and account takeover

name: Fraud Prevention Policy

context: To establish fraud prevention procedures that: Detect unauthorized transactions (fraud), Block fraudulent activity before settlement, Reimburse customers fairly for fraud losses, Investigate fraud cases, Prevent repeat fraud by same perpetrator

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: Unauthorized transactions representing fraudulent activity that the policy is designed to detect, block, and investigate. This is a primary risk category addressed by the fraud prevention procedures.

name: Unauthorized Transaction Detection
description: Mandatory requirement to detect unauthorized transactions as part of fraud prevention procedures. This provision establishes the obligation to identify fraudulent activity.

name: Fraudulent Activity Blocking Before Settlement
description: Mandatory requirement to block fraudulent activity before settlement occurs. This provision establishes the obligation to prevent fraudulent transactions from completing.

name: Customer Reimbursement for Fraud Losses
description: Mandatory requirement to reimburse customers fairly for fraud losses incurred. This provision establishes the obligation to provide financial redress to affected customers.
context: Reimburse customers fairly for fraud losses

name: Fraud Case Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement to investigate fraud cases. This provision establishes the obligation to conduct thorough investigations into suspected fraudulent activity.

name: Repeat Fraud Prevention by Same Perpetrator
description: Mandatory requirement to prevent repeat fraud by the same perpetrator. This provision establishes the obligation to implement measures that stop identified fraudsters from committing further fraud.
context: Prevent repeat fraud by same perpetrator

name: Customer

name: Fraud Detection Obligation
description: The operational obligation to detect and identify unauthorized transactions and fraudulent activity as part of the fraud prevention framework.

name: Fraud Investigation

name: Customer Reimbursement

context: Reimburse customers fairly for fraud losses

name: Fraud Protection Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's overarching policy framework for protecting customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation. The policy establishes the bank's commitment to fraud prevention and customer protection.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation.

name: Fraud
description: The risk of fraudulent transactions or unauthorized account activity that the bank's detection and monitoring systems are designed to identify and prevent.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation.

name: Fraud Detection System
description: Operational safeguard deployed by FirstUK Bank to identify and flag fraudulent transactions and suspicious account activity.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation.

name: Real-Time Transaction Monitoring
description: Continuous monitoring mechanism that analyzes customer transactions in real-time to detect and prevent fraudulent activity.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation.

name: Fair Liability Allocation for Fraud
description: Policy provision establishing the bank's framework for fairly allocating liability between the bank and customers in fraud scenarios, ensuring equitable treatment and protection.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation.

name: Customer
description: Natural persons who hold accounts and banking relationships with FirstUK Bank and are protected by the bank's fraud prevention measures.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customers from fraud through detection systems, real-time transaction monitoring, and fair liability allocation.

name: Authorized Fraud
description: A fraud scenario where a customer authorizes a transaction but subsequently claims fraud. The customer is typically liable for losses if negligence is demonstrated, except in cases of fraud perpetrated by bank staff or unauthorized card use. This category encompasses situations where customers knowingly provide transaction details or authorization to criminals.
context: Customer authorizes transaction but later claims fraud
Customer liable for loss IF customer negligent
Exception: Fraud by staff member or unauthorized card use

name: Customer Impersonation of Bank
description: A fraud scenario in which a customer is deceived by a criminal impersonating a bank representative and authorizes a transaction based on this false representation. The customer calls what they believe to be their bank but is actually communicating with a criminal.
context: Customer calls "bank" (actually criminal) and authorizes transfer

name: Card Detail Disclosure to Fraudster
description: A fraud scenario where a customer discloses card details to a third party claiming to be bank support staff. The customer is deceived into providing sensitive payment card information to a criminal.
context: Customer gives card details to stranger claiming to be support

name: Investment Scam Wire Transfer
description: A fraud scenario in which a customer authorizes a wire transfer to a criminal posing as an investment opportunity provider. The customer is deceived into transferring funds based on false investment promises.
context: Customer wire transfers to criminal "investment opportunity"

name: Debit Card
description: A payment card referenced in the context of unauthorized use fraud scenarios. The policy establishes that customers are not liable for losses resulting from unauthorized card use by third parties.
context: Exception: Fraud by staff member or unauthorized card use

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds a bank account and is subject to fraud liability provisions. The customer's negligence, authorization decisions, and disclosure of account details are material to fraud liability determination.
context: Customer authorizes transaction but later claims fraud
Customer liable for loss IF customer negligent

name: Authorized Transfer
description: A financial transfer initiated by a customer that is later disputed as fraudulent. The transaction is authorized by the customer but may be claimed as fraud if the customer was deceived or negligent.
context: Customer authorizes transaction but later claims fraud
Customer calls "bank" (actually criminal) and authorizes transfer

name: Wire Transfer
description: A wire transfer transaction authorized by a customer to a recipient. In fraud scenarios, customers may authorize wire transfers to criminals based on false investment opportunities or other deceptive representations.
context: Customer wire transfers to criminal "investment opportunity"

name: Customer Liability for Authorized Fraud
description: A provision establishing that customers are liable for losses resulting from authorized fraud transactions if the customer was negligent. The provision creates an exception where customers are not liable if the fraud was perpetrated by bank staff or involved unauthorized card use.
context: Customer liable for loss IF customer negligent
Exception: Fraud by staff member or unauthorized card use

name: Unauthorized Fraud Liability Policy
description: Policy defining FirstUK Bank's liability and reimbursement obligations for unauthorized fraud scenarios where customers did not authorize transactions and criminals obtained access through compromised credentials or physical theft. The policy establishes zero customer liability if reported within 24 hours and mandates 100% bank reimbursement within 10 business days.
context: Criminal uses account without customer authorization
FirstUK Bank reimburses 100% of unauthorized loss

name: Zero Customer Liability for Unauthorized Fraud
description: Provision establishing that customers bear zero financial liability for unauthorized fraud transactions provided they report the incident to the bank within 24 hours of discovery.

name: Full Reimbursement of Unauthorized Loss
description: Provision requiring FirstUK Bank to reimburse customers 100% of losses resulting from unauthorized fraud transactions, establishing the bank's full liability for such incidents.
context: FirstUK Bank reimburses 100% of unauthorized loss

name: Reimbursement Processing Timeframe
description: Provision mandating that FirstUK Bank must process and complete reimbursement of unauthorized fraud losses within 10 business days of the claim being validated.

name: Gross Negligence Exception to Zero Liability
description: Provision establishing that customer zero-liability protection may be forfeited if the customer is found to have acted with gross negligence in safeguarding their credentials or account access.

name: Unauthorized Account Access
description: Risk category covering scenarios where criminals gain unauthorized access to customer accounts through theft of credentials, physical cards, or social engineering attacks such as phishing, enabling fraudulent transactions without customer authorization.
context: Criminal uses account without customer authorization
Criminal obtained access (stolen password, card, etc.)

name: Card Cloning
description: Risk category covering fraudulent duplication of payment card data, typically at ATMs or point-of-sale terminals, enabling unauthorized transactions on cloned cards.

name: Unauthorized Card Fraud Event
description: Fraud scenario where a customer's payment card is stolen and subsequently used by a criminal to conduct unauthorized transactions, triggering bank liability and customer reimbursement obligations.

name: Unauthorized Online Transfer Fraud Event
description: Fraud scenario where a customer's online banking password is compromised, enabling criminals to conduct unauthorized electronic transfers from the customer's account.

name: Account Takeover Fraud Event
description: Fraud scenario where criminals gain control of a customer account through phishing attacks or other social engineering methods, enabling unauthorized access and fraudulent transactions.

name: Card Cloning Fraud Event
description: Fraud scenario where a customer's card data is cloned at an ATM or similar terminal, enabling criminals to create duplicate cards and conduct unauthorized transactions.

name: Fraud Victim Customer
description: Customer who is the victim of unauthorized fraud, having not authorized transactions conducted on their account by criminals who obtained unauthorized access through stolen credentials or physical theft.
context: Criminal obtained access (stolen password, card, etc.)

name: Debit Card
description: Payment card subject to unauthorized fraud risk, including scenarios of theft and criminal use, as well as cloning at ATMs.

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: Financial transaction conducted on a customer account without the customer's authorization, initiated by a criminal who obtained unauthorized access to the account.
context: Criminal uses account without customer authorization

name: Card Not Present Fraud
description: Fraudulent online purchases where card details are stolen through website hacking or data breaches. Bank liability depends on the strength of authentication mechanisms employed during the transaction.
context: Bank liability depends on authentication strength

name: Card Present Fraud
description: Fraudulent transactions where a physical card is used by a thief, typically after the card has been stolen from the customer. The bank is liable for losses unless the customer was negligent.

name: Card Cloning
description: Fraudulent scheme where card details are copied from a legitimate card and used to create a counterfeit card. The bank is liable for losses that occur after the customer reports the fraud.
context: Card details copied from legitimate card

name: Debit Card
description: Payment card subject to fraud scenarios including Card Not Present fraud, Card Present fraud, and card cloning as described in the policy.
context: Card details copied from legitimate card

name: Card Fraud Event
description: Detection and response to fraudulent card transactions across three primary scenarios: Card Not Present fraud, Card Present fraud, and card cloning. Response obligations and bank liability vary by fraud type and customer conduct.
context: Card details copied from legitimate card

name: Account Takeover
description: A financial crime scenario in which a criminal gains unauthorized access to a legitimate customer account through compromise of authentication credentials or security mechanisms. The document defines account takeover as a criminal gaining access via password, security questions, or other authentication factors, and specifies the bank's mandatory response procedures.
context: Criminal gains access to legitimate account (password, security questions)

name: Account Takeover Detection and Response
description: The bank's mandatory operational response to a detected or suspected account takeover event, including immediate account freeze, forced password reset, credential review, multi-factor authentication re-verification, and full reimbursement of customer losses.

name: Immediate Account Freeze
description: An emergency protective control requiring immediate suspension of account access upon detection or reasonable suspicion of account takeover, preventing further unauthorized transactions.

name: Forced Password Reset
description: A mandatory control requiring the customer's password to be reset immediately following account takeover detection, invalidating any compromised credentials.

name: Security Question Credential Review
description: A verification control requiring review and re-establishment of security question answers and other credential-based authentication factors following account takeover.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication Re-verification
description: A control requiring customers to re-verify and re-enroll in multi-factor authentication mechanisms following account takeover, ensuring attacker-compromised MFA channels are replaced.

name: Full Reimbursement of Account Takeover Losses
description: A mandatory provision requiring the bank to reimburse customers in full for all financial losses resulting from confirmed account takeover incidents, regardless of customer negligence in credential protection.

name: Phishing Attack
description: A social engineering attack vector used to compromise customer credentials, specifically through fraudulent emails containing fake login pages designed to capture authentication credentials.

name: Third-Party Data Breach Password Compromise
description: A risk scenario where customer passwords are compromised through data breaches at third-party organizations, enabling attackers to attempt unauthorized access to bank accounts using leaked credentials.

name: Social Engineering Attack
description: A fraud attack vector in which criminals impersonate bank customer support staff to manipulate customers into revealing authentication credentials or account access information.

name: SIM Swap Attack
description: A sophisticated attack vector in which criminals intercept SMS-based two-factor authentication by fraudulently transferring the victim's phone number to a SIM card under attacker control, bypassing SMS 2FA protections.

name: Malware on Customer Device
description: A threat vector in which malicious software installed on a customer's personal device enables attackers to capture credentials, intercept authentication codes, or monitor account activity.

name: Fraud Detection Framework
description: A comprehensive policy governing the bank's fraud detection methods, including real-time transaction monitoring, manual review procedures, and advanced pattern analysis. The framework establishes detection rules, alert generation protocols, and continuous model improvement through machine learning feedback loops.

name: Real-Time Transaction Monitoring
description: Mandatory requirement to monitor all transactions in real-time using the Fraud Detection Engine (FDE-001) against a defined set of fraud detection rules. Transactions meeting alert criteria are placed on hold for up to 5 days pending review.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

name: Large Transaction Amount Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting for transactions exceeding £5,000. This rule is part of the real-time transaction monitoring framework.

name: Velocity Check Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a customer initiates more than 5 transactions within a 1-hour period. This rule identifies potentially fraudulent rapid transaction patterns.

name: Geographic Anomaly Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a transaction occurs in a different country within 2 hours of a previous transaction. This rule identifies impossible travel scenarios.
context: Geographic anomaly (transaction in different country within 2 hours)

name: New Beneficiary Large Transfer Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a customer initiates a large transfer to a newly added beneficiary. This rule identifies potential account compromise or fraud.

name: Unusual Merchant or Category Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting for transactions with unusual merchant types or spending categories that deviate from customer's normal behavior.

name: Cash Withdrawal Followed by Large Transfer Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a cash withdrawal is immediately followed by a large transfer. This rule identifies potential money laundering or fraud patterns.
context: Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer

name: Multiple Failed Authentication Attempts Detection Rule
description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when multiple failed authentication attempts occur on an account. This rule identifies potential account takeover attempts.

name: Transaction Hold on Fraud Alert
description: Mandatory requirement to place transactions on hold for up to 5 days when a fraud alert is generated by the Fraud Detection Engine, pending manual review and approval.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

name: Manual Review of Suspected Fraud
description: Mandatory requirement for the Financial Crime team to manually investigate transactions triggered by customer fraud reports, unusual account activity, pattern changes, high-value transactions, or regulatory alerts. Customer contact for explanation is required when safe to do so.
context: Transaction approved or blocked based on risk

name: Machine Learning Model Training on Confirmed Fraud
description: Mandatory requirement to update the machine learning fraud detection model with confirmed fraud cases to continuously improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives.

name: Fraud Detection Engine
description: Real-time automated system that monitors all transactions against defined fraud detection rules including large amounts, velocity checks, geographic anomalies, new beneficiaries, unusual merchants, and authentication failures. Generates alerts and places flagged transactions on hold.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

name: Machine Learning Fraud Pattern Analysis
description: Advanced analytics control that uses machine learning to learn normal customer behavior patterns, flag anomalies for review, identify recurring fraud patterns, and track fraud perpetrators across multiple customers. The model is continuously refined based on confirmed fraud feedback.
context: Machine learning model learns normal customer behavior

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The Financial Crime team is responsible for conducting manual investigations of fraud alerts and suspicious activities, analyzing customer activity, contacting customers for explanations when safe to do so, and making transaction approval or blocking decisions based on risk assessment.
context: Transaction approved or blocked based on risk

name: Fraud
description: The primary risk category addressed by this policy. Fraud encompasses unauthorized transactions, account takeover, new beneficiary fraud, velocity-based fraud, geographic anomalies, and other deceptive activities that the detection framework is designed to identify and prevent.

name: Account Takeover
description: A specific fraud risk where unauthorized parties gain control of a customer account, typically identified through multiple failed authentication attempts and unusual transaction patterns.

name: Money Laundering
description: A financial crime risk identified through the detection of cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer patterns, which may indicate attempts to obscure the origin of funds.
context: Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer

name: Fraud Detection Alert
description: An automated alert generated by the Fraud Detection Engine when a transaction meets one or more fraud detection rules. The alert triggers transaction hold and manual review by the Financial Crime team.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

name: High-Value Transaction
description: Transactions exceeding £5,000 that are subject to real-time monitoring and fraud detection rules. These transactions are flagged for potential fraud review.

name: Rapid Velocity Transaction
description: Multiple transactions (more than 5) initiated within a 1-hour period that trigger fraud detection alerts due to unusual velocity patterns.

name: Geographic Anomaly Transaction
description: A transaction occurring in a different country within 2 hours of a previous transaction, flagged as a geographic anomaly that may indicate fraud or account compromise.
context: Geographic anomaly (transaction in different country within 2 hours)

name: New Beneficiary Transfer
description: A large transfer to a newly added beneficiary that is subject to fraud detection monitoring and manual review.

name: Cash Withdrawal Followed by Large Transfer
description: A transaction pattern consisting of a cash withdrawal immediately followed by a large transfer, flagged as a potential money laundering or fraud indicator.
context: Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer

name: Customer Fraud Reporting Policy
description: Policy governing the process by which customers report suspected fraud, the bank's immediate response actions, investigation procedures, and reimbursement decisions. Establishes timelines for investigation (24–48 hours) and reimbursement (within 10 days if fraud is confirmed).

name: Customer Fraud Report Submission
description: Customers must be able to report suspected fraud via multiple channels: phone (0800-555-2265), email, branch, or online. Full details, timeline, and amounts must be captured.

name: Immediate Account Freeze on Account Takeover
description: Upon receipt of a customer fraud report involving account takeover, the account must be frozen immediately as part of the response protocol.

name: Immediate Card Block on Card Fraud
description: Upon receipt of a customer fraud report involving card fraud, the affected card must be blocked immediately as part of the response protocol.

name: Fraud Report Escalation to Financial Crime Team
description: All customer fraud reports must be escalated to the Financial Crime team as part of the immediate response procedure.

name: Temporary Access Provision During Fraud Investigation
description: Customers reporting fraud must be provided with temporary access to funds or services via an alternate card or account while the investigation is ongoing.

name: Fraud Investigation Completion Timeline
description: Fraud investigations must be completed within 24–48 hours, including review of transaction details, fraud likelihood assessment, payment status check, liability determination, and documentation of findings.

name: Confirmed Fraud Reimbursement Obligation
description: When fraud is confirmed following investigation, the customer must receive full reimbursement within 10 days.
context: If Fraud Confirmed: Full reimbursement within 10 days

name: Non-Fraud Finding Communication and Education
description: When investigation determines the reported transaction is not fraud, the bank must explain the reasoning to the customer and provide education.
context: If Not Fraud: Explain reasoning, educate customer

name: Disputed Fraud Finding Escalation
description: When a customer disputes the fraud investigation finding, the matter must be escalated to the Head of Financial Crime with follow-up action.
context: If Disputed: Escalate to Head of Financial Crime + follow-up

name: Account Takeover
description: A fraud scenario in which an unauthorized party gains control of a customer's account, triggering immediate account freeze and investigation procedures.

name: Card Fraud
description: A fraud scenario involving unauthorized use of a customer's payment card, triggering immediate card block and investigation procedures.

name: Fraud Report Acknowledgment
description: Immediate acknowledgment of customer fraud reports upon receipt, establishing the start of the investigation and response process.

name: Transaction Detail Review
description: Detailed review of transaction records as part of the fraud investigation process to assess the validity of the customer's fraud claim.

name: Fraud Likelihood Assessment
description: Evaluation of the likelihood that reported transactions constitute fraud, based on investigation findings and transaction patterns.

name: Payment Status Verification
description: Verification of the status of payments involved in the reported fraud to determine whether funds have been settled or can be recovered.

name: Fraud Liability Determination
description: Assessment and determination of liability for the fraudulent transaction, establishing whether the bank or customer bears responsibility.

name: Fraud Investigation Documentation
description: Comprehensive documentation of all fraud investigation findings, decisions, and supporting evidence for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The team responsible for receiving escalated fraud reports from customer-facing staff and conducting the investigation into suspected fraud within the defined 24–48 hour timeframe.

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior role responsible for escalation and final decision-making in disputed fraud cases where the customer contests the investigation outcome.
context: Escalate to Head of Financial Crime + follow-up

name: Customer Fraud Report
description: The formal process initiated when a customer reports suspected fraud via phone, email, branch, or online channels, triggering immediate response actions and investigation.

name: Confirmed Fraud Reimbursement
description: The outcome of a fraud investigation where fraud is confirmed, resulting in full reimbursement to the customer within 10 days.
context: If Fraud Confirmed: Full reimbursement within 10 days

name: Customer
description: The individual customer who reports suspected fraud and is the subject of the investigation and reimbursement decision process.

name: Debit Card
description: A payment card issued to a customer that may be subject to fraud and blocked immediately upon report of card fraud.

name: Customer Account
description: A customer account that may be subject to account takeover fraud and is frozen immediately upon such report, with temporary access provided via alternate means.

name: Liability and Reimbursement Policy
description: Policy governing customer liability for unauthorized transactions, account takeover, and fraud scenarios. Establishes three liability tiers: zero liability (bank pays all), reduced liability (customer pays part), and full customer liability (customer pays all), with specific conditions and reporting timeframes for each.

name: Zero Liability for Unauthorized Card Use
description: Bank assumes full liability for unauthorized card use when the customer reports the incident within 24 hours of discovery. This provision protects customers from financial loss in cases of card fraud.
context: Unauthorized card use (if reported within 24 hours)

name: Zero Liability for Account Takeover
description: Bank assumes full liability for account takeover when it is not the customer's fault. This provision protects customers from unauthorized access to their accounts.

name: Zero Liability for Stolen Check or Account Details
description: Bank assumes full liability when stolen checks or account details are used fraudulently. This provision covers scenarios where customer information is compromised without customer action.

name: Zero Liability for Bank Impersonation Scam
description: Bank assumes full liability when a customer is tricked by a fraudster impersonating the bank. This provision protects customers who are socially engineered into unauthorized transactions.
context: Scam (customer tricked by fraudster impersonating bank)

name: Reduced Liability for Gross Negligence
description: Customer bears partial liability when gross negligence is demonstrated, such as writing a password on a card. This provision establishes shared responsibility when customer security practices are severely deficient.
context: Gross negligence (e.g., writing password on card)

name: Reduced Liability When Customer Knew Fraudster
description: Customer bears partial liability when the fraudster was known to the customer. This provision reflects reduced bank responsibility when the customer had a prior relationship with the perpetrator.

name: Reduced Liability for Delayed Fraud Reporting
description: Customer bears partial liability when fraud is reported more than 24 hours after discovery. This provision incentivizes prompt reporting to minimize bank losses and fraud exposure.

name: Full Customer Liability for Authorized Transactions
description: Customer bears full liability for transactions they authorized, even if they later regret the transaction. This provision establishes that authorization is binding and non-reversible absent fraud or error.
context: Authorized transaction (customer authorized but later regrets)

name: Full Customer Liability for Negligent Security Practices
description: Customer bears full liability when negligence in security practices is demonstrated, such as writing down passwords or sharing card details. This provision holds customers accountable for basic security hygiene.

name: Full Customer Liability for Unauthorized Access Breach
description: Customer bears full liability when they grant unauthorized persons access to their account or card. This provision establishes that customers are responsible for controlling who has access to their banking credentials.
context: Breach of security (unauthorized person given access)

name: Unauthorized Card Use
description: Risk of fraudulent use of a customer's payment card by an unauthorized party. The policy addresses this through a 24-hour reporting window and zero liability for the customer when promptly reported.
context: Unauthorized card use (if reported within 24 hours)

name: Account Takeover
description: Risk of unauthorized access to and control of a customer's account by a third party. The policy provides zero liability protection when the takeover is not attributable to customer fault.

name: Stolen Check or Account Details Fraud
description: Risk of fraudulent use of stolen checks or compromised account details. The policy provides zero liability protection when the customer's information is misused without their authorization.

name: Bank Impersonation Scam
description: Risk of customer being deceived by a fraudster impersonating the bank into authorizing unauthorized transactions. The policy provides zero liability protection for customers who are victims of such social engineering.
context: Scam (customer tricked by fraudster impersonating bank)

name: Unauthorized Card Use Detection
description: Detection and response obligation for unauthorized card transactions. The policy establishes a 24-hour reporting window within which customers must notify the bank to receive zero liability protection.
context: Unauthorized card use (if reported within 24 hours)

name: Account Takeover Detection
description: Detection and response obligation for unauthorized account access. The policy provides zero liability protection when the takeover is determined to be outside the customer's control.

name: Debit Card
description: Payment card subject to unauthorized use liability provisions. The policy establishes zero liability for unauthorized card use when reported within 24 hours.
context: Unauthorized card use (if reported within 24 hours)

name: Customer
description: Individual customer holding a bank account and subject to liability provisions for unauthorized transactions, fraud, and negligent security practices. The policy establishes tiered liability based on customer actions and reporting timeliness.

name: Bank Account
description: Customer account subject to unauthorized access, takeover, and fraud scenarios covered by the liability and reimbursement policy. The policy establishes liability tiers based on the nature of the unauthorized activity.
context: Breach of security (unauthorized person given access)

name: Unauthorized Card Fraud
description: Fraudulent use of a customer's card without authorization. The bank is liable for reimbursement within 10 business days of discovery.

name: Account Takeover
description: Unauthorized access and control of a customer account by a third party. The bank is liable for reimbursement within 10 business days.

name: Fraudulent Transfer
description: Unauthorized transfer of funds from a customer account. Bank liability applies when the Faster Payment System (FPS) has not yet settled, with reimbursement due within 10 business days.
context: Fraudulent transfer | Bank (if FPS not settled) | 10 business days

name: Scam
description: A scenario where a customer is tricked or deceived into authorizing a fraudulent transaction. The bank is liable for reimbursement within 10 business days.

name: Customer Negligence
description: Fraudulent activity resulting from customer negligence or failure to exercise reasonable care. The customer is liable and receives no reimbursement.

name: Unauthorized Card Fraud Reimbursement
description: Bank liability and reimbursement obligation for unauthorized card fraud, with a 10 business day reimbursement timeline.

name: Account Takeover Fraud Reimbursement
description: Bank liability and reimbursement obligation for account takeover fraud, with a 10 business day reimbursement timeline.
